item.title: India’s Dollar Hedging Slumps as RBI Cracks Down on Speculation
item.description: Indian companies cut dollar purchases used to hedge against rupee weakness to an eight-month low, a sign that the central bank’s crackdown on what it called speculative bets against the currency is yielding results.

item.title: Corn Extends Loss to Hit Four-Month Low on Supply, Peace Hopes
item.description: Chicago corn extended losses, hitting the lowest in four months, as an outlook for ample US supply and prospects for peace in the Black Sea region weighed on prices.

item.title: Temasek’s Mapletree Is Said to Pick Banks for Singapore IPO
item.description: Mapletree Investments Pte, a real estate firm owned by Singapore state investor Temasek Holdings Pte, has picked banks for an initial public offering of parts of the company in the city state that could raise at least S$1 billion ($780 million), according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Asian Stocks Fall as Democratic Gains in US Add to AI Worries
item.description: Asian stocks fell to their lowest in over six months after early victories by the Democrats in the US midterm elections fueled concerns about tighter oversight of the artificial intelligence industry.

item.title: China Services Gauge Unexpectedly Dips for First Time Since July
item.description: China’s services activity unexpectedly grew at a slower rate for the first time since July, a private survey showed, as business confidence eased and firms lowered their selling prices despite intensifying inflation in input costs.
